hypothesis: K=RP3 x S1 is a configuration/menu space of global gluing and phase sectors, not necessarily a literal compact spatial manifold.

nonabelian_obstruction.theorem: Finite-dimensional unitary representations of the abelian group Z2 x Z are simultaneously diagonalizable and split into one-dimensional characters.
nonabelian_obstruction.interpretation: Using noncommuting Pauli generators violates the defining commutativity relation of pi1(K); nonabelian particle multiplets require an extra fiber, groupoid or operator algebra not contained in K alone.

coherent_state_menu.finding: K can consistently be reinterpreted as a label space for global gluing, spin and holonomy sectors rather than as a literal compact spatial dimension.

discrete_plus_cyclic_labels.finding: Stable loop classes carry one integer winding and one Z2 torsion label, matching the minimal idea of charge plus parity.

nonabelian_multiplets_from_base_topology.finding: pi1(K) is abelian. Every finite-dimensional unitary holonomy representation decomposes into one-dimensional characters, so irreducible SU(2) doublets and SU(3) triplets cannot come from base-loop holonomy alone.

three_generation_selection.finding: The natural discrete counts are 2 flat components, 4 spin structures and 8 components in the enlarged spin-holonomy menu; none canonically selects 3.

mass_spectrum_from_topology_alone.finding: Topology labels sectors but supplies no energy, stiffness or transition operator. Masses require an additional metric/action on the menu.

scientific_verdict.survives: The hypothesis is mathematically coherent as a kinematic classification of global phase, torsion and spin sectors.
scientific_verdict.fails: It cannot by itself generate nonabelian gauge multiplets, three generations, masses or dynamics.
scientific_verdict.minimal_extension: Replace the bare menu by a nonabelian bundle/groupoid over the two-circle moduli, with a preregistered transition operator and metric.
scientific_verdict.next_gate: Test whether one minimal nonabelian fiber can produce both an SU(2) doublet and an SU(3) triplet without adding independent sector choices.
